ownership_reason: Only the gold decides which nodes are examined and whether a node carries text: it walks the subtree of the element depth first, without recursion, from the last child node back, and tests each text node with isBlank. Hops 1, 3 and 4 pass the element along; hop 2 only answers false for an element without child nodes. The gold returns a boolean, so once its walk has moved past the searched element into the nodes before it, no caller can undo that or tell where the text was found. The gold's javadoc promises the facade's contract (the node has text content that is not just whitespace); the second div of the trigger has none, and the variant answers true from the text of the first div. The convention that a search of an element covers only its subtree is pinned outside the gold: the intact NodeTraversor.traverse and NodeTraversor.filter do the same walk without recursion and stop at the root (climbing only while depth > 0, then `if (node == root)`), used in production by Element.text() over `this`; TraversorTest::filterVisit and ElementsTest::traverse pass (each div's walk stays inside that div), as do, through the chain, ElementTest::testHasText and ElementsTest::eachText.
